reason: I'll start the protected colon wall by putting mucus on the lining; the picture shows it as a layer above those cells.

effect: The remaining goal is complete: bacteria break down some leftover fibre and release small fatty acids and gas.
reaction: The gas was a surprise, and the result answered what the microbes make, though not how they break fibre down.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the inner wall was worthwhile because it connected the protective layers to water recovery and showed that bacterial products can fuel lining cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mucus was straightforward but mostly confirmed the picture, without much new information.

surprise.text: I didn't expect fibre breakdown by resident bacteria to produce gas as well as small fatty acids.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the cecal junction appeared as a new, unexplained term when the tract was connected.

continue.text: I would continue: seeing how the colon's layers and microbes do different jobs made me curious about other body systems.
